description.short_caption: CT scan of the abdomen showing a hypodense lesion in the liver.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the abdomen demonstrates a hypodense lesion in the liver, likely in the right lobe. The lesion appears well-circumscribed and distinct from the surrounding liver parenchyma. Adjacent structures, including the kidneys and bowel, are visible but appear unremarkable. The scan is performed with contrast, as evidenced by the enhancement of vascular structures.
visible_findings: normal appearance of kidneys and bowel

description.short_caption: Abdominal ultrasound showing a hypoechoic lesion with measurements.
description.detailed_description: This is an abdominal ultrasound image showing a hypoechoic lesion in the liver. The lesion is measured with calipers, indicating dimensions of approximately 7.82 cm by 7.33 cm. The surrounding liver parenchyma appears heterogeneous. The image is de-identified and includes a scale bar and measurement annotations.

description.short_caption: CT scan of the abdomen showing a hypodense lesion in the liver.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the abdomen demonstrates a hypodense lesion in the liver, likely in the right hepatic lobe. The lesion appears well-demarcated and may represent an abscess or other pathological process. Surrounding liver parenchyma appears relatively normal. The scan is performed without visible contrast enhancement, and the vertebral body is visible posteriorly for orientation.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing air-fluid levels and abnormal gas distribution.
description.detailed_description: This is an upright chest radiograph displaying the thoracic cavity and upper abdomen. Notable findings include air-fluid levels in the left hemithorax, suggestive of a diaphragmatic hernia or bowel perforation with pneumothorax. The lung fields appear asymmetrical, with the left side showing reduced aeration. The gastric bubble is visible, and there is abnormal gas distribution in the upper abdomen. The bony structures, including the ribs and spine, appear intact.
visible_findings: air-fluid levels in the left hemithorax
reduced aeration in the left lung
abnormal gas distribution in the upper abdomen
